title: Tilt-Shift
description: Tilt-shift cinematography tilts the lens relative to the sensor so the plane of focus rotates, and may also shift the lens to slide perspective. A narrow band or shaped region of sharpness, often from a high viewpoint, can make a real-scale scene resemble a small model.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Tilt is not a blur sticker. The Scheimpflug relation puts a slice of the world in focus along a plane that is no longer parallel to the sensor: a street of rowers, a crowd, a tabletop of people who suddenly read as toys.
Shift is a different job: it slides the image to keep verticals parallel or to look around a corner without rotating the camera. It is the wrong tool when you only wanted a face isolated from a wall.
That is Shallow Focus on a normal plane. It is also the wrong tool if the miniature effect has no high viewpoint and no consistent focus band.
A horizontal blur strip that ignores perspective is a post fake, not this optic.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Tilt the lens so the focus plane cuts through the subject as a thin band or a wedge. A high angle helps the diorama reading because we look down on models.
Match blur to depth; as perspective changes, the band should follow the plane, not a 2D stripe. Shift independently if you need to correct converging buildings.
Prompt: A real-scale city or citadel with [Subject] human-sized. A thin band of focus across the subject, foreground and far ground softly blurred, no hard seam across the frame.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it to make a city a model, or to slice focus through a crowd on a tilted plane. Do not use it as a synonym for shallow portrait focus, and do not lay a blur bar across a flat image.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Shallow Focus keeps the focus plane parallel to the sensor and isolates by distance. Tilt rotates that plane.
Macro is close-up scale, not a diorama of a city. Bird's-Eye View can supply the high viewpoint the miniature reading often needs, but a bird's-eye without a tilted focus plane is just a map.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: The Social Network's Henley rowing sequence gives real-scale action a miniature-like appearance through a thin, high, diorama focus. Miniature-city treatments in other films follow the same grammar: high view, shallow band, motion that reads like a toy.
Borrow the plane, not a still of the race.

sections.title: Prompt it

blocks.text: Name real scale, then the thin focus plane. A real-scale city or citadel with [Subject] human-sized.
A thin horizontal band of focus across the subject, foreground and far ground softly blurred, no hard seam across the frame. Add a high viewpoint if you want the diorama.
Do not write shallow bokeh portrait, and do not ask for a hard blur stripe.

High oblique view of two rowing teams moving along a river, with a narrow depth-aware focus region around the boats and smoothly increasing blur nearer and farther away. Slightly brisk motion and crisp miniature-like detail. No actual toy proportions, no arbitrary blurry stripe across faces.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is Shallow Focus on a face, or a post miniature with a 2D blur strip. The tell is a portrait with creamy background, or a seam that ignores buildings' depth.
Fix: high view, human-sized figures, focus as a plane through the scene, blur that follows depth.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is tilt-shift in film?

Tilt rotates the plane of focus relative to the sensor. Shift slides the lens to change perspective without tilting the camera. Together they can isolate a band of sharpness or make real scenes read as models.
Tilt-Shift vs Shallow Focus

Shallow focus keeps the focus plane parallel to the sensor and falls off with distance. Tilt-shift can put a wedge or band of focus through a scene, including a high diorama view of a city. Blur shape is the difference.
When should I use tilt-shift?
Use it to slice focus through a crowd or to turn real-scale action into a model. Skip it for ordinary portraits that only need a fast 85mm.
How do I prompt tilt-shift for AI image or video?
Write that the subject is human-sized in a real city, with a thin band of focus and no hard seam. Add a high viewpoint for the diorama. Forbid a flat blur stripe and ordinary portrait bokeh.
